segments.text: You point your coding agent at one button, but most changes have unforeseen consequences. What if you took every page and component of your UI and laid them out next to each other? Now, let's copy those components into every state the user will see. Error states, empty states, easy ones, hard ones. Storybook JS has made that easy for the past 10 years. With coding agents, it's more useful than ever. You can point at the specific page you want changed. But how can you understand the full ripples of a code change? Enter Chromatic. This is a cloud service which renders every component of a storybook to an image. Change the code, render every component to another image, and compare. This works great, but it requires waiting on a cloud service. At 0.8 cents per image, this was a reasonable expense at the speed of human code. But for a modest library of 1,000 stories, that's eight bucks for a full run each time you even look at a code change. Introducing selfie.dev, a snapshot testing tool which runs locally and in the cloud. Your agent takes its own picture. No waiting on a cloud rendering service and no paying for each image. 541 stories in about 70 seconds. It works just like Git. Images are stored locally wherever the agent is running and also in the cloud, so that every commit on GitHub shows the complete visual consequences of the code change. Approvals follow your history too, so they survive a commit, a rebase, or a merge. Every image is rendered in the same pinned environment, wherever it runs. Each image is named by a hash of its pixels. Most changes touch only a few, so only those few get sent. If you're using Storybook JS, you can start using Selfie locally to review your changes right now at selfie.dev. If you want to use it in the cloud on your GitHub repositories, join our waitlist and get a discount when we launch in mid-November.
